clue.text: Copper taken in by missing stripper?

indicators.note: something taken in by another is held inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: missing means lost
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman is detained by a striptease artist who has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' wants to be a police officer and 'stripper' a performer; in fact the definition is a creature that strips crops bare, signalled by the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Swarming insects of this kind devour every leaf in a field, so they are fanciful strippers of vegetation.

clue.text: Product of Bologna — a sort of square vessel

indicators.note: a product of something is made out of it, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: a T-square is a sort of square used by draughtsmen

explanation.surface: An Italian city makes a kind of square boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Product of' rearranges BOLOGNA into LONGBOA.
explanation.definitionFit: A long rowing boat carried by a sailing ship, or a Viking ship, is a type of vessel.

clue.text: Keep secret report at university

parts.note: to cover a story is to report it
up means at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A news report from a university is kept quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: Being UP is British usage for being at university.
explanation.definitionFit: To conceal a scandal or keep it from becoming known is a synonym.

clue.text: A tourist greets his constituents

indicators.note: constituents are the parts something is made from, so these letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A tourist says hello to his voters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents' rearranges GREETS HIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist goes about looking at famous places, a visitor to the attractions.

clue.text: Business area still on cloud nine

parts.note: EC (East Central) is the postal district of the City of London, its business district
still means motionless, static

explanation.surface: Someone in the business district stays put but is overjoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the London postcode for the City, Britain's financial quarter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on cloud nine is an idiom for being blissfully happy, which is the sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Newman, for one, calls attention to directions

parts.note: John Henry Newman was a cardinal of the Roman Catholic Church
points means calls attention to something

explanation.surface: A churchman draws attention to the way to go.
explanation.walkthrough: Newman was the nineteenth-century English theologian made a cardinal.
explanation.definitionFit: North, south, east and west are the four main compass directions.

clue.text: It's encountered around Togo's borders, erected as an emblem

indicators.note: erected means set upright, so in a down entry the letters are read from the bottom up
around means surrounding, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: encountered means met

indicators.note: the borders of the word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An emblem raised near the frontiers of Togo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' builds the word forwards first; 'erected' then turns the whole of it, because in a down light raising means reading upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved pole or object symbolising a clan or tribe is its emblem.

clue.text: Catch up on most of the procedure for the shoot

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece
up in a down clue means the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: to net a fish is to catch it

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is lost

parts.note: the drill is the established procedure

explanation.surface: Get up to date with nearly all the rules for a photo shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns NET into TEN; DRILL loses its last letter to give DRIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing plant sends out a thin curling shoot to grip a support.

clue.text: Where the ship-builder first learns his trade?

definitions.text: Where the ship-builder first learns his trade?

parts.words: Where the ship-builder first learns his trade?
parts.note: a frame that supports a hull while it is built, and also a baby's bed, where any worker starts out

explanation.definitionFit: A baby's cot is where life starts, and in shipyards a framework holds a vessel under construction.

clue.text: Hint made girl turn white in London street

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the girl and the shuffled colour go within the street

parts.note: the Strand is a famous street in central London
Win is a girl's name, short for Winifred

indicators.note: turn means change about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clue that caused a girl to go pale in a London thoroughfare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' rearranges WHITE into THEWI; 'made' is only a link. The Strand runs from Trafalgar Square to Fleet Street.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sign of which way things are going is an idiom for a hint.

clue.text: Aviator no good perhaps as a map-reader

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters may be arranged differently from how they stand

explanation.surface: A pilot who is no good might be the one reading the map instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' shuffles AVIATOR together with NG.
explanation.definitionFit: The crew member who plots the route of a plane or ship reads the maps and charts.

clue.text: Island's holy books rejected by printers

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, is a set of holy books
NGA was the National Graphical Association, the British printers' trade union

explanation.surface: The scriptures of some island have been turned down by the printing firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns OT into TO; the 's of 'Island's' is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Pacific kingdom made up of many islands, often called an island nation.

clue.text: Cloth cap?

parts.note: reads like a flat cap of fabric, but 'the cloth' is the clergy, so it is a cap worn by priests

explanation.definitionFit: A square ecclesiastical headdress worn by Roman Catholic clergy, the men of the cloth.

clue.text: Incorruptible leader of 11 abandoned? Abandoned for sure!

indicators.note: abandoned means given up, so the named letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: incorruptible in the sense of not subject to decay, everlasting, is immortal
the first letter of the answer to 11 across is T

explanation.surface: An upright head of an island state has been deserted, and is utterly depraved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for sure!' is an emphatic tag on the definition: abandoned in the sense of wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoned can mean wildly dissolute and unrestrained, which is a synonym for wicked or depraved.

clue.text: Quite enough drink to drown a member

indicators.note: to drown something is to submerge it, so one piece is engulfed by the other

parts.note: ale is a drink
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: There is plenty to drink to drown a politician in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drown' suggests the member is submerged in the drink, which is exactly the container picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Plentiful or sufficient: having more than enough is a synonym.

clue.text: Drab colour for a Castilian queen

definitions.meaning: a greyish-yellow shade, said to be named after the dingy linen of a Spanish princess
the queen of Castile who sponsored Columbus

explanation.surface: A dull shade of paint chosen for a Spanish monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both that of the fifteenth-century monarch of Castile and of a dull buff hue.

clue.text: Zamenhof hoped it would make neat prose

definitions.text: Zamenhof hoped it would make neat prose

indicators.note: make means form something new, so these letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: The inventor of a language wanted it to give tidy writing.
explanation.walkthrough: Ludwik Zamenhof created the international language whose name is NEAT PROSE rearranged by 'make'.
explanation.definitionFit: The artificial language devised by Zamenhof in 1887, which he hoped would become universal.

clue.text: Where brothers and sisters can be sent for a walk?

definitions.text: Where brothers and sisters can be sent for a walk?

parts.words: Where brothers and sisters can be sent for a walk?
parts.note: siblings sounds like a family outing, but these are monks and nuns, who walk round a covered arcade

explanation.definitionFit: A covered arcade round a monastery courtyard is where monks and nuns walk.

clue.text: Go too far in measure taken : after deliveries

indicators.note: after places the measure behind the deliveries in the answer

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries, so overs are deliveries
a step is a measure, a course of action

explanation.surface: A bowler oversteps the mark after delivering the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deliveries' is cricket language: an OVER is a set of six balls bowled.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstep a line is an idiom for exceeding a limit, going beyond what is allowed.

clue.text: Nourishment soldiers on motorway found in French wine

indicators.note: found in means placed inside, so the soldiers and motorway go within the wine

parts.note: vin is French for wine

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve soldiers
the M1 is Britain's main motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: Food for troops found on a motorway in a glass of French wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 runs from London to Leeds; its name is read as the letters MI.
explanation.definitionFit: An essential organic compound in the diet is a component of nourishment.

clue.text: One who is taught to be indispensable to 3?

definitions.meaning: the opening in the eye's iris, which a tourist at 3 down needs to see

explanation.surface: A learner must be essential to the person in clue 3.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a cross-reference: a part of the eye is vital to someone whose job is looking.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a schoolchild being taught and the dark circular opening at the centre of the eye.

clue.text: Bicoloured bird lacking feathers

parts.note: pie is an old name for the magpie, a bird
lacking feathers means bald

explanation.surface: A two-toned bird has lost its plumage.
explanation.walkthrough: The magpie is black and white, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse with patches of black and white is described by this adjective, meaning two-coloured.

clue.text: Many supporting a museum, or one wrecking it?

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed underneath the other piece

parts.note: the V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London
L is the Roman numeral 50, many

explanation.surface: Lots of people supporting a museum, or someone smashing it up?
explanation.walkthrough: The V and A, spelt out as VANDA, is London's museum of decorative arts.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who wilfully damages property is a wrecker of it.

clue.text: The object of literary composition.

definitions.meaning: the definite ... is a part of speech of this kind
a piece of writing in a newspaper or magazine

explanation.surface: The aim of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: 'The' is itself an example, 'object' means an item, and a written piece in a paper is one too.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers a grammatical term like a or an, a thing or item, and a piece of journalism.

clue.text: Western state without an inland waterway

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California, a western US state

explanation.surface: A western state lacks an inland waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking but means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificial channel for boats inland is a waterway.

clue.text: In the Middle' East he lives with artist and priest

parts.note: lives means exists, is
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
Eli was the priest who raised Samuel in the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A man in the Middle East lives with a painter and a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: a man of the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of the Jewish state on the eastern Mediterranean is a man of the Middle East.

clue.text: A fiend put on about 50% of them

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to put on clothes is to don them

indicators.note: 50% of a four-letter word is two of its letters, here the second half

explanation.surface: A devil dresses up in roughly half of their clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: '50% of' picks the back half of THEM, two of its four letters; 'put on' is the verb for dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: An evil spirit or devil is a synonym for a fiend.

clue.text: Mean worker made manager overseas:

parts.note: to mean to do something is to intend it
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: A stingy employee was promoted to boss abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' pretends to be stingy but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: In France and elsewhere abroad it is the title of an administrator, such as the director of an opera house.

clue.text: Eg Mrs Bardell's day out with two students?

parts.note: L is the learner plate abbreviation, so two students give L twice
with means and
the second of the two learner letters

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Mrs Bardell takes a day off with a couple of trainees.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Bardell is Mr Pickwick's landlady in Dickens's novel; 'out' rearranges DAY into ADY. The 's reads 'Mrs Bardell is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs Bardell lets rooms to Mr Pickwick in The Pickwick Papers, which makes her an example of a woman who rents out lodgings.

clue.text: Join up and serve in the Army if one short

indicators.note: short means lacking, so one letter is left out

parts.note: to soldier is to serve in the army
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Enlist and do military service if one is short of a recruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Join up' wants to mean enlist, which fits the army surface, but it means fuse metal.
explanation.definitionFit: To fuse metal parts together with molten alloy is to join them.
